top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, B048) is the only substantive proposal on the slate. It rests on an identifiable originating model, Melitz (2003), with Helpman's exporting-versus-FDI work as a tightly linked extension, so credit divides cleanly between two names. Its qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years. The disputes concern welfare magnitudes and functional form, not the mechanism. The main reservation is priority: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed parallel firm-level facts and models. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework addresses this only partly. The reservation is not serious enough to prefer no award. I do not count the number of supporters, the 2008 trade prize or field rotation as evidence of merit. P000 is ranked last because the work meets the criteria of discovery, maturity and attribution.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Melitz or Helpman. My field of political science (institutions and their measurement) is outside the proposal's field, and no connection to the credited names is documented in my profile.
